name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 21 points
Incumbent David Taylor has a large fundraising edge while no fundraising is reported for his challenger
Prediction markets price the Democrat near 1 percent
No public polls or expert ratings, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: An R+21 district, a well-funded incumbent seeking re-election against a challenger with no reported fundraising, and markets pricing the Democrat at roughly 1 percent all align; the seat rates as Safe Republican.
model.watch: Only a major incumbent scandal, a late surge of challenger fundraising, or a sharp national shift toward Democrats would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-02 is a heavily Republican district in southern Ohio, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. Republican David Taylor holds the seat and is running for re-election, while Democrat Jennifer Mazzuckelli is the party's nominee. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race.

The evidence on hand points firmly to the incumbent. Taylor has raised about $1.1 million and enters the fall with roughly $443,000 on hand, while no fundraising totals are reported for his challenger. Prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a 1 percent chance of winning. With the district's strong Republican lean, the incumbent's financial advantage, and no visible signs of competition, the forecast rates the race Safe Republican.
